definition.body: The terminal bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the most distal airway of the purely conducting portion of the bronchial tree, the airway immediately proximal to the respiratory bronchiole. Parameters: (1) the position in the conducting path — the final rung of the accepted airway hierarchy, the path running subsegmental bronchus, terminal bronchiole, respiratory bronchiole, alveolar duct, alveolar sac, alveolus, so the terminal bronchiole is the last airway before the respiratory zone begins; (2) the wall architecture — a smooth-muscle and elastic-fiber sleeve without hyaline cartilage plates and without submucosal glands, its wall perforated by no alveolar openings, which is the map's boundary: the first wall to carry scattered alveolar outpouchings is already the respiratory bronchiole; (3) the epithelial lining — simple cuboidal epithelium with ciliated and Club cells at this distal limit, the last fully ciliated airway; (4) the caliber — under 1 mm internal diameter, below the subsegmental level whose cartilage plates mark the bronchial side of the transition; (5) the functional role — the last airway contributing to conducting-zone airway resistance, so its smooth-muscle tone sets the threshold below which obstruction is a small-airways disease rather than a bronchial one. payload.name: terminal-bronchiole
payload.scope: People made the terminal-bronchiole construct to map the most distal purely conducting airway, so that histologists can identify the boundary between conducting and respiratory zones and clinicians can assess small-airways disease.

definition.body: The terminal bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the most distal purely conducting airway in the respiratory tree, terminating at the transition to the respiratory zone. Parameters: (1) the position in the hierarchy - branching from each subsegmental bronchus and giving rise to one or two respiratory bronchioles, approximately the 15th to 16th generation from the trachea; (2) the wall architecture - a thin-walled tube without cartilage or submucosal glands, lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with ciliated cells and Clara (club) cells that secrete surfactant-like material and detoxify inhaled substances; (3) the smooth-muscle component - a relatively thick circumferential smooth muscle layer that can significantly narrow the lumen, making terminal bronchioles the primary site of airway resistance in the conducting zone; (4) the functional boundary - the last airway generation with no alveolar outpouchings in its wall, immediately proximal to the respiratory bronchiole where gas exchange begins. It persists as a maintained landmark in pulmonary histology, respiratory physiology, and occupational lung disease assessment. e.g.: the terminal bronchiole as described in Junqueira Basic Histology, 15th edition; small-airways disease assessment by methacholine challenge testing per ATS guidelines; the terminal bronchiole as the site of centrilobular emphysema in West Respiratory Physiology, 10th edition | not: the respiratory bronchiole (the transitional airway where alveolar outpouchings first appear in the wall); the subsegmental bronchus (the proximal cartilage-bearing airway, a generation more central) [formal: bronchiolus terminalis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

definition.body: The terminal bronchiole is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the most distal purely conducting airway in the respiratory tree, terminating at the transition to the respiratory zone. Parameters: (1) the position in the hierarchy - branching from each subsegmental bronchus and giving rise to one or two respiratory bronchioles, approximately the 15th to 16th generation from the trachea; (2) the wall architecture - a thin-walled tube without cartilage or submucosal glands, lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with ciliated cells and Clara (club) cells that secrete surfactant-like material and detoxify inhaled substances; (3) the smooth-muscle component - a relatively thick circumferential smooth muscle layer that can significantly narrow the lumen, making terminal bronchioles the primary site of airway resistance in the conducting zone; (4) the functional boundary - the last airway generation with no alveolar outpouchings in its wall, immediately proximal to the respiratory bronchiole where gas exchange begins. It persists as a maintained landmark in pulmonary histology, respiratory physiology, and occupational lung disease assessment. e.g.: the terminal bronchiole as described in Junqueira Basic Histology, 15th edition; small-airways disease assessment by methacholine challenge testing per ATS guidelines; the terminal bronchiole as the site of centrilobular emphysema in West Respiratory Physiology, 10th edition | not: the respiratory bronchiole (the transitional airway where alveolar outpouchings first appear in the wall); the subsegmental bronchus (the proximal cartilage-bearing airway, a generation more central) [formal: bronchiolus terminalis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
